html:
The War of the Heavenly Horses was a war that the Han dynasty of China fought against Dayuan, a kingdom in the Fergana Valley, between 104 and 102 BCE. The prize was horses.

The envoy Zhang Qian had reported that Dayuan bred tall, strong "blood sweating" horses. Emperor Wu wanted them for his cavalry against the Xiongnu. When Dayuan refused to trade them and killed a Han envoy, he sent an army under the general Li Guangli.

The first campaign failed: the army crossed the deserts of the Tarim Basin, lost most of its men to hunger and thirst, and turned back. In 102 BCE a much larger army set out. It besieged Dayuan's capital and cut off its water. The nobles killed their king and made peace, handing over dozens of the finest horses and about three thousand others.

The war cost China dearly, but it showed that Han power could reach across Central Asia. The oasis kingdoms of the Tarim Basin began to send tribute, and the routes later called the Silk Road came under Chinese protection.
